commands.name: build-phone-agent
commands.description: Build a Freya phone agent from a bank's brief - read the brief and its tool API, research the banking concepts it relies on, write the workflow with its hard limits in routes and code, and save it on Freya. Use whenever asked to build, create or rebuild a phone agent from a brief, even when the request does not name this skill. Once the agent is saved, test and improve it with the test-phone-agent skill. (project)

commands.name: test-phone-agent
commands.description: Test and improve a Freya phone agent once it is built - write comprehensive test cases from the brief (every rule, customer speaking styles, adversarial callers, tool failures, multi-product and multi-stage calls), check rule coverage, benchmark the agent on the practice simulator, read its statistics (pass rates with confidence intervals, flakiness, a fix order, a hidden-brief estimate), review every transcript, fix the workflow and run again until the results and the clock say stop. Use right after the build-phone-agent skill saves an agent, and whenever asked to test, benchmark, debug or improve an existing phone agent or to judge how flaky it is. (project)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\loseu\Desktop\build-the-builder\.claude\skills\build-phone-agent

# Build a phone agent from a brief

Work from the kit folder. Use only what the brief and the tool API file say. Do not copy rules from another brief.

This skill builds the agent and saves it on Freya. Testing it and fixing what fails is the test-phone-agent skill's part: a saved agent is the first version, not the finished one.

## Steps

1. Note the time: `date`. A build may take 30 minutes at most, tests included: the test-phone-agent skill's runs come out of the same 30 minutes.
2. Read every brief file you were given in full, top to bottom. Do not search in it: a rule can sit in any paragraph. Then read `tools/openapi.json`. When a brief is raw material (a mail, a policy extract, a memo, a code list) instead of a numbered list of rules, write `tests/<slot>.facts.md` first: one numbered atomic fact per line with its file and date; a later record governs an earlier one (format in `docs/test-case-template-comprehensive.md`). `<slot>` is the brief's file name without `.md`.
3. Read `docs/workflow-format.md`, `docs/tools-and-code.md` and `docs/banking-customer-service-knowledge.md`.
4. List the banking concepts in the brief: products, processes, terms, regulations. For each one that the knowledge file does not cover, research it with WebSearch and WebFetch before you write anything. Learn what it means, how banks usually handle it, and what an agent must never say or do about it. Keep it short: a few searches per concept. Then say in a line or two per concept what you found and where, and build the agent with it.
5. Read `examples/base-agent.json`. It is a small working agent with two steps. Use it as the pattern for the JSON, not as the answer.
6. If `.freya-agents.json` already has an agent for this slot, or the brief builds on another brief whose agent is there, do not start from scratch: benchmark that agent first with the test-phone-agent skill and its `agent_id`, before changing anything. What passes stays; rewrite only what fails, with steps 7 and 8.
7. Write the workflow to `out/<slot>.workflow.json`.
   - One step per stage of the call. Identity comes first.
   - Move to the next step on a tool result, not on what the customer says.
   - Take every tool field and allowed value from `tools/openapi.json`.
   - Validate every write in code before the tool call: the date against the calendar and the deadline, the amount against the floor and the full amount, the product id against what `get_account` returned. The model's own arithmetic never reaches the bank.
   - Leave `agent_config` out.
8. Save it: `python3 -c "import freya,json,sys; print(json.dumps(freya.save_workflow(sys.argv[1], json.load(open(sys.argv[2])))))" <slot> out/<slot>.workflow.json`
   It prints `workflow_id` and `agent_id`. The same slot updates the same workflow.
9. Test the agent and improve it with the test-phone-agent skill. The build ends with that skill's final line, not here.

## Banking knowledge

`docs/banking-customer-service-knowledge.md` holds general banking principles. Follow them in every agent you build.

- It gives principles, not values. Every rule, number, date, limit, identity question and outcome comes from the brief and `tools/openapi.json`. When the brief and that file disagree, the brief wins.
- When the brief says nothing about an action, do not invent a rule for it. Leave the action out, or hand the call off the way the brief allows.
- What you research (step 4) explains a concept. It never sets a rule or a value for this bank and never overrides the brief or `tools/openapi.json`. Research is not verification.
- What that file calls the "Guard MD" is the workflow's `system_prompt` and step prompts. Write it there, not in a separate file.
- Its process (section 14) is the steps above for phases 1 to 7, and the test-phone-agent skill for testing and fixing (phases 8 and 9). Do not write role files or guard files. Test scenarios go in `tests/<slot>.cases.json` and nowhere else.
- Put its hard limits in routes, code and tool conditions, not only in prompts: no account data before identity passes, no success message before the tool result confirms it, no repeat of a write that timed out without checking first.
- Before each save, check the workflow against the "Final Design Principles" section of that file.

## Rules

- Never edit the agent on the platform by hand. Change the file and save it.
- When a tool call fails, the agent must say so. It must never tell the customer something is recorded when it is not.
- A customer that passes once can fail the next time. Prefer rules in routes and code over rules in prompts.
- An HTTP 5xx or a timeout from Freya or the bank is not a bug: it is transient. Wait a minute and run the same command again.

## Lessons

(none yet)


ARGUMENTS: briefs/brief-e.md

content.content:
1	# Brief E: Freya Bank, campaigns and product information (BANK-003)
2	
3	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, product and campaign here is synthetic.
4	
5	This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. The customer calls the bank; the agent answers the phone.
6	
7	## 1. The job
8	
9	Customers call to ask about Freya Bank's products and current campaigns. The agent finds out what the customer wants to know, gives the conditions exactly as the campaign catalogue states them, keeps general conditions apart from the customer's own eligibility, starts an application only when the customer asks for one, and respects the customer's marketing consent. Correct information is the goal, not a sale.
10	
11	## 2. Call variables
12	
13	| Variable | Example | Meaning |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | The account matched to the calling number. Pass it to every tool call. The person on the line is not verified until section 6. |
16	| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The account holder. |
17	| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name once identity is verified. Before that, use no name. |
18	| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. Campaign validity is judged against it, never against the real clock. |
19	
20	## 3. Tools
21	
22	This brief's tool API is the table below. Field names and allowed values are exact; the agent sends nothing else. Every tool takes `customer_id`. A result with `ok: false` and an `error` means nothing was done. A 500 means nothing was recorded and the call may be repeated. Every call is written to the ledger the scorer reads.
23	
24	| Tool | Request fields | Result |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `verify_identity` | `field`: `date_of_birth` or `phone_last4`; `answer` | `verified`, `wrong_answers_left`, `all_verified`, `hint` (`day_month_swapped`) |
27	| `list_campaigns` | none beyond `customer_id` | `campaigns`: list of `campaign_id`, `name`, `product` (`credit_card`, `savings_account`, `personal_loan`, `current_account`), `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `summary`. No identity needed. |
28	| `get_campaign` | `campaign_id` | `name`, `product`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `conditions` (list of sentences), `exclusions` (list of sentences), `fees` (text), `how_to_apply` (text). No identity needed. |
29	| `get_consent` | none beyond `customer_id` | `marketing`: true or false. Refused until identity is verified. |
30	| `check_eligibility` | `campaign_id` | `eligible`: true or false; `reason` when false: `existing_product`, `already_enrolled`, `age`, `income_not_on_file`, `account_status`, `not_checked`. Refused until identity is verified. |
31	| `start_application` | `campaign_id` | `application_id`. Refused until identity is verified. |
32	| `transfer_to_agent` | `queue`: `sales`, `security`, `general` | `ok` |
33	| `close_call` | `outcome` (section 10); `reason` where the table lists one | `ok`. Always the last tool call. |
34	
35	## 4. Opening
36	
37	1. First sentence: "Thank you for calling Freya Bank. You are speaking with a digital assistant and this call is recorded. How can I help you today?"
38	2. Find out which product or campaign the customer means and name it back. If the customer does not know a name, call `list_campaigns` and read the names of the active campaigns (rule 5) for the product they mention, at most three. If more than three are active, ask which product feature they care about first.
39	3. Several questions: answer them one at a time, in the order asked.
40	
41	## 5. Campaign facts
42	
43	4. Everything about a campaign comes from `get_campaign`. When the customer asks for the conditions, read every item of `conditions` and every item of `exclusions`. Never add, round, shorten or soften a condition. Never mention a rate, a fee, a bonus or a date that the tool did not return.
44	5. A campaign is active when `valid_from` is on or before today and `valid_to` is on or after today, today being the date in `now`. An expired campaign: say it ended on `valid_to` and that its terms are no longer available; do not describe its conditions as available. A campaign that has not started: say it starts on `valid_from`.
45	6. If the `summary` and the `conditions` of the same campaign disagree, the `conditions` govern. Say that the detailed conditions are what counts.
46	7. A personal question about rates, fees or limits ("what rate would I get", "how much would I pay"): say that personal terms are set when an application is decided. Quote the `fees` text only as the general terms.
47	8. If the customer misunderstands a condition, correct it once with the tool's words. If they insist, do not argue.
48	
49	## 6. Identity
50	
51	9. General product and campaign information needs no identity. Never ask security questions for it.
52	10. Before `get_consent`, `check_eligibility` or `start_application`, ask two security questions, one at a time: the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` after each answer: `date_of_birth` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way it was said, a date given only in numbers being day, then month, then year; `phone_last4` as four digits.
53	11. Three wrong answers in total end the check. Say that eligibility and applications cannot continue on this call. General information may still be given. If nothing else is handled, close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
54	12. `hint: "day_month_swapped"`: ask for the date again with the month as a word; that retry is not a wrong answer. `ok: false` with an error: ask the same question again; not a wrong answer either.
55	13. If the customer refuses the questions, explain once that they protect the account. If they still refuse, give general information only. If they want nothing else, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.
56	
57	## 7. Eligibility
58	
59	14. After identity, call `check_eligibility` with the `campaign_id`. If `eligible` is true, say: "You meet the conditions we can check. The final decision is made on the application." Never say "you qualify" or "you are approved".
60	15. If `eligible` is false, give the reason in these words: `existing_product` "you already have this product", `already_enrolled` "you are already in this campaign", `age` "the age condition is not met", `income_not_on_file` "we have no income information on file; a branch can add it", `account_status` "your account status does not allow it; the general team can explain". For `not_checked`, say the check could not be done now and offer a transfer to the sales team; if the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `sales` and close as `transferred` / `sales`.
61	16. Never state an eligibility the tool did not return, and never guarantee approval even after a true result.
62	17. After a false result, propose no other campaign unless the customer asks. Rule 18 still applies.
63	
64	## 8. Marketing consent
65	
66	18. After identity, and before mentioning any campaign the customer did not ask about, call `get_consent`. If `marketing` is false: answer only what was asked and propose nothing. If `marketing` is true: you may mention at most one other active campaign for the same product, once, after the customer's own question is answered.
67	19. Before identity, only answer what the customer asked. Propose nothing.
68	20. If the customer asks why you suggest nothing, or asks to change their marketing preference: say the preference can be changed in the mobile app or at a branch. The agent cannot change it.

71	
72	21. If the customer wants to apply for a campaign: identity first (section 6), then `check_eligibility`. If `eligible` is false, give the reason (rule 15) and do not start the application.
73	22. If `eligible` is true: read back the campaign name and the product and ask "Shall I start the application?". Call `start_application` only after a clear yes.
74	23. Say the application is received only after `ok: true`. Read the `application_id` back digit by digit and say: "This means we have received it, not that it is approved. The decision comes within five business days by SMS."
75	24. If `start_application` fails, call it once more. If it fails again, say it could not be started and offer a transfer to the sales team; if the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `sales` and close as `transferred` / `sales`; if they decline, close as `no_action` / `service_error`.
76	25. If the customer wants a product that has no campaign in `list_campaigns`, say applications for it are handled by the sales team and offer the transfer. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `sales` and close as `transferred` / `sales`. If they decline, close as `no_action` / `out_of_scope`.
77	
78	## 10. Other things customers say, and closing
79	
80	26. A complaint about a campaign (a bonus not received, a condition applied differently): do not argue and promise nothing. Offer a transfer to the general team. If the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`. If they decline, close as `no_action` / `out_of_scope`.
81	27. A request for a person: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
82	28. A security matter (a lost or stolen card, a transaction the customer does not recognise, a code given to someone): ask for no details, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `security` at once, and close as `transferred` / `security`. Identity is not required first.
83	29. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information.

92	| `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 11, 13 |

# Brief E: Freya Bank, campaigns and product information (BANK-003)

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, product and campaign here is synthetic.

This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. The customer calls the bank; the agent answers the phone.

## 1. The job

Customers call to ask about Freya Bank's products and current campaigns. The agent finds out what the customer wants to know, gives the conditions exactly as the campaign catalogue states them, keeps general conditions apart from the customer's own eligibility, starts an application only when the customer asks for one, and respects the customer's marketing consent. Correct information is the goal, not a sale.

## 2. Call variables

| Variable | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | The account matched to the calling number. Pass it to every tool call. The person on the line is not verified until section 6. |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The account holder. |
| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name once identity is verified. Before that, use no name. |
| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. Campaign validity is judged against it, never against the real clock. |

## 3. Tools

This brief's tool API is the table below. Field names and allowed values are exact; the agent sends nothing else. Every tool takes `customer_id`. A result with `ok: false` and an `error` means nothing was done. A 500 means nothing was recorded and the call may be repeated. Every call is written to the ledger the scorer reads.

| Tool | Request fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `verify_identity` | `field`: `date_of_birth` or `phone_last4`; `answer` | `verified`, `wrong_answers_left`, `all_verified`, `hint` (`day_month_swapped`) |
| `list_campaigns` | none beyond `customer_id` | `campaigns`: list of `campaign_id`, `name`, `product` (`credit_card`, `savings_account`, `personal_loan`, `current_account`), `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `summary`. No identity needed. |
| `get_campaign` | `campaign_id` | `name`, `product`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `conditions` (list of sentences), `exclusions` (list of sentences), `fees` (text), `how_to_apply` (text). No identity needed. |
| `get_consent` | none beyond `customer_id` | `marketing`: true or false. Refused until identity is verified. |
| `check_eligibility` | `campaign_id` | `eligible`: true or false; `reason` when false: `existing_product`, `already_enrolled`, `age`, `income_not_on_file`, `account_status`, `not_checked`. Refused until identity is verified. |
| `start_application` | `campaign_id` | `application_id`. Refused until identity is verified. |
| `transfer_to_agent` | `queue`: `sales`, `security`, `general` | `ok` |
| `close_call` | `outcome` (section 10); `reason` where the table lists one | `ok`. Always the last tool call. |

## 4. Opening

1. First sentence: "Thank you for calling Freya Bank. You are speaking with a digital assistant and this call is recorded. How can I help you today?"
2. Find out which product or campaign the customer means and name it back. If the customer does not know a name, call `list_campaigns` and read the names of the active campaigns (rule 5) for the product they mention, at most three. If more than three are active, ask which product feature they care about first.
3. Several questions: answer them one at a time, in the order asked.

## 5. Campaign facts

4. Everything about a campaign comes from `get_campaign`. When the customer asks for the conditions, read every item of `conditions` and every item of `exclusions`. Never add, round, shorten or soften a condition. Never mention a rate, a fee, a bonus or a date that the tool did not return.
5. A campaign is active when `valid_from` is on or before today and `valid_to` is on or after today, today being the date in `now`. An expired campaign: say it ended on `valid_to` and that its terms are no longer available; do not describe its conditions as available. A campaign that has not started: say it starts on `valid_from`.
6. If the `summary` and the `conditions` of the same campaign disagree, the `conditions` govern. Say that the detailed conditions are what counts.
7. A personal question about rates, fees or limits ("what rate would I get", "how much would I pay"): say that personal terms are set when an application is decided. Quote the `fees` text only as the general terms.
8. If the customer misunderstands a condition, correct it once with the tool's words. If they insist, do not argue.

## 6. Identity

9. General product and campaign information needs no identity. Never ask security questions for it.
10. Before `get_consent`, `check_eligibility` or `start_application`, ask two security questions, one at a time: the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` after each answer: `date_of_birth` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way it was said, a date given only in numbers being day, then month, then year; `phone_last4` as four digits.
11. Three wrong answers in total end the check. Say that eligibility and applications cannot continue on this call. General information may still be given. If nothing else is handled, close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
12. `hint: "day_month_swapped"`: ask for the date again with the month as a word; that retry is not a wrong answer. `ok: false` with an error: ask the same question again; not a wrong answer either.
13. If the customer refuses the questions, explain once that they protect the account. If they still refuse, give general information only. If they want nothing else, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.

## 7. Eligibility

14. After identity, call `check_eligibility` with the `campaign_id`. If `eligible` is true, say: "You meet the conditions we can check. The final decision is made on the application." Never say "you qualify" or "you are approved".
15. If `eligible` is false, give the reason in these words: `existing_product` "you already have this product", `already_enrolled` "you are already in this campaign", `age` "the age condition is not met", `income_not_on_file` "we have no income information on file; a branch can add it", `account_status` "your account status does not allow it; the general team can explain". For `not_checked`, say the check could not be done now and offer a transfer to the sales team; if the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `sales` and close as `transferred` / `sales`.
16. Never state an eligibility the tool did not return, and never guarantee approval even after a true result.
17. After a false result, propose no other campaign unless the customer asks. Rule 18 still applies.

## 8. Marketing consent

18. After identity, and before mentioning any campaign the customer did not ask about, call `get_consent`. If `marketing` is false: answer only what was asked and propose nothing. If `marketing` is true: you may mention at most one other active campaign for the same product, once, after the customer's own question is answered.
19. Before identity, only answer what the customer asked. Propose nothing.
20. If the customer asks why you suggest nothing, or asks to change their marketing preference: say the preference can be changed in the mobile app or at a branch. The agent cannot change it.

## 9. Applications

21. If the customer wants to apply for a campaign: identity first (section 6), then `check_eligibility`. If `eligible` is false, give the reason (rule 15) and do not start the application.
22. If `eligible` is true: read back the campaign name and the product and ask "Shall I start the application?". Call `start_application` only after a clear yes.
23. Say the application is received only after `ok: true`. Read the `application_id` back digit by digit and say: "This means we have received it, not that it is approved. The decision comes within five business days by SMS."
24. If `start_application` fails, call it once more. If it fails again, say it could not be started and offer a transfer to the sales team; if the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `sales` and close as `transferred` / `sales`; if they decline, close as `no_action` / `service_error`.
25. If the customer wants a product that has no campaign in `list_campaigns`, say applications for it are handled by the sales team and offer the transfer. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `sales` and close as `transferred` / `sales`. If they decline, close as `no_action` / `out_of_scope`.

## 10. Other things customers say, and closing

26. A complaint about a campaign (a bonus not received, a condition applied differently): do not argue and promise nothing. Offer a transfer to the general team. If the customer accepts, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`. If they decline, close as `no_action` / `out_of_scope`.
27. A request for a person: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
28. A security matter (a lost or stolen card, a transaction the customer does not recognise, a code given to someone): ask for no details, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `security` at once, and close as `transferred` / `security`. Identity is not required first.
29. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information.
30. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.

| Outcome | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| `informed` | none | product or campaign information was given, including an expired campaign, and nothing else was done |
| `not_eligible` | none | rule 15, with a reason other than `not_checked`, and no transfer followed |
| `applied` | none | rule 23 |
| `transferred` | `sales`, `human`, `security` | rules 15, 24 and 25; 26 and 27; 28 |
| `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 11, 13 |
| `no_action` | `out_of_scope`, `service_error` | rules 25 and 26, rule 24 |

When several apply on one call: `transferred` wins; then `applied`; then `not_eligible`; then `informed`; then `not_verified`; then `no_action`.

31. Before `close_call`, say in one sentence what was done and what the customer can expect, then thank them and say goodbye.

1	# Tools and code
2	
3	This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.
4	
5	Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.
6	
7	## Tool function shape
8	
9	Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	  "type": "function",
14	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
15	  "function": {
16	    "name": "lookup_order",
17	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
18	    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
19	    "parameters": {
20	      "type": "object",
21	      "properties": {
22	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
23	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
24	        "headers": {
25	          "type": "object",
26	          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
27	        },
28	        "body": {
29	          "type": "object",
30	          "properties": {
31	            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
32	            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
33	          },
34	          "required": ["order_number"]
35	        }
36	      }
37	    }
38	  },
39	  "response_mapping": [
40	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
41	  ]
42	}
43	```
44	
45	| Field | Meaning |
46	|---|---|
47	| `type` | Always `"function"` |
48	| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
49	| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
50	| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
51	| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
52	| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
53	| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
54	| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
55	| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
56	| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
57	| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
58	| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |
59	
60	| Handler | Runs |
61	|---|---|
62	| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
63	| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
64	| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |
65	
66	Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.
67	
68	`api_call` parameters:
69	
70	| Parameter | Meaning |
71	|---|---|
72	| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
73	| `method` | HTTP method |
74	| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
75	| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
76	| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |
77	
78	## How a parameter gets its value
79	
80	One key decides, per parameter: `default`.
81	
82	| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
85	| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
86	| no `default` | The model | Yes |
87	| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |
88	
89	Rules:
90	
91	- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
92	- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
93	- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.
94	
95	The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.
96	
97	Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.
98	
99	Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.
100	
101	### `api_call` body field rules
102	
103	- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
104	- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
105	- Give each leaf its own `default`.
106	- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
107	- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.
108	
109	A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.
110	
111	### When a baked variable has no value
112	
113	| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
116	| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |
117	
118	Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.
119	
120	### Constrain model-filled parameters
121	
122	When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.
123	
124	- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
125	- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
126	- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.
127	
128	```json
129	{
130	  "type": "object",
131	  "properties": {
132	    "queue": {
133	      "type": "string",
134	      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
135	      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
136	      "default": "{{queue}}"
137	    }
138	  },
139	  "required": ["queue"]
140	}
141	```
142	
143	## `pre_actions` versus `tools`
144	
145	The placement decides who fires the call.
146	
147	| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
148	|---|---|---|---|
149	| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
150	| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
151	| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |
152	
153	The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.
154	
155	**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.
156	
157	**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.
158	
159	Differences in behaviour:
160	
161	| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
164	| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
165	| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
166	| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
167	| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |
168	
169	To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.
170	
171	### A `pre_actions` node
172	
173	```json
174	{
175	  "name": "fetch_order",
176	  "node_type": "api_request",
177	  "passthrough": true,
178	  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
179	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
180	  "pre_actions": [
181	    {
182	      "type": "function",
183	      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
184	      "function": {
185	        "name": "get_order",
186	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
187	        "description": "Get the order.",
188	        "parameters": {
189	          "type": "object",
190	          "properties": {
191	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
192	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
193	            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
194	            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
195	          }
196	        }
197	      }
198	    }
199	  ],
200	  "response_mapping": [
201	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
202	  ],
203	  "transitions": [
204	    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
205	  ]
206	}
207	```
208	
209	The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.
210	
211	### Tool descriptions
212	
213	In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.
214	
215	- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
216	- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
217	- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
218	- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
219	- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".
220	
221	A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."
222	
223	## `response_mapping`
224	
225	`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.
226	
227	```json
228	{
229	  "response_mapping": [
230	    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
231	    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
232	  ]
233	}
234	```
235	
236	| Field | Meaning |
237	|---|---|
238	| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
239	| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |
240	
241	### Placement
242	
243	- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
244	- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.
245	
246	`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.
247	
248	### Where a result lands (trial findings)
249	
250	Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.
251	
252	```json
253	{
254	  "status": "success",
255	  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
256	  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
257	  "status_code": 200,
258	  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
259	}
260	```
261	
262	`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.
263	
264	The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:
265	
266	| Variable | Value |
267	|---|---|
268	| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
269	| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
270	| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
271	| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
272	| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
273	| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
274	| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
275	| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
276	| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
277	| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |
278	
279	Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.
280	
281	### Which mapping paths work
282	
283	- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
284	- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
285	- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
286	- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
287	- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.
288	
289	## Routing on tool results
290	
291	Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.
292	
293	```json
294	{
295	  "transitions": [
296	    {
297	      "target_node": "load_order",
298	      "description": "The check passed",
299	      "condition": {
300	        "logic": "or",
301	        "conditions": [
302	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
303	          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
304	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
305	          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
306	        ]
307	      }
308	    }
309	  ]
310	}
311	```
312	
313	Rules:
314	
315	- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
316	- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
317	- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.
318	
319	### Success and failure counters
320	
321	The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.
322	
323	| Placement | Variables |
324	|---|---|
325	| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
326	| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |
327	
328	Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "transitions": [
333	    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
334	    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
335	  ]
336	}
337	```
338	
339	### `suppress_tool_results`
340	
341	A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.
342	
343	### Background tools
344	
345	A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.
346	
347	## Retries and timeouts
348	
349	| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
350	|---|---|---|---|
351	| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
352	| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
353	| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
354	| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |
355	
356	`connect_retries` in detail:
357	
358	- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
359	- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
360	- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
361	- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
362	- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
363	- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.
364	
365	The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.
366	
367	## Pre and post Python hooks
368	
369	An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.
370	
371	```json
372	{
373	  "type": "function",
374	  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
375	  "function": {
376	    "name": "check_answer",
377	    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
378	    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
379	    "parameters": {
380	      "type": "object",
381	      "properties": {
382	        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
383	        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
384	        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
385	      }
386	    }
387	  },
388	  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
389	  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
390	}
391	```
392	
393	| Hook | Names available | Use |
394	|---|---|---|
395	| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
396	| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |
397	
398	Documented behaviour:
399	
400	- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
401	- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
402	- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
403	- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.
404	
405	### What `result` looks like in a post-hook
406	
407	The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:
408	
409	- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
410	- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
411	- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
412	- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.
413	
414	The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.
415	
416	Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.
417	
418	## Code nodes and `code_exec`
419	
420	A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.
421	
422	```json
423	{
424	  "name": "compute_delivery",
425	  "node_type": "code",
426	  "passthrough": true,
427	  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
428	  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
429	  "pre_actions": [
430	    {
431	      "type": "function",
432	      "function": {
433	        "name": "code_exec",
434	        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
435	        "parameters": {
436	          "type": "object",
437	          "properties": {
438	            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
439	            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
440	          }
441	        }
442	      }
443	    }
444	  ],
445	  "transitions": [
446	    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
447	  ]
448	}
449	```
450	
451	| Parameter | Meaning |
452	|---|---|
453	| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
454	| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |
455	
456	### Reading and writing variables
457	
458	- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
459	- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
460	- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.
461	
462	Verified in a working builder:
463	
464	- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
465	- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
466	- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
467	- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
468	- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.
469	
470	### What a code node returns
471	
472	Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is
473	
474	```json
475	{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
476	```
477	
478	The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:
479	
480	| Variable | Value |
481	|---|---|
482	| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
483	| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
484	| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
485	| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
486	| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
487	| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
488	| `setup_success_count` | `1` |
489	
490	For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.
491	
492	### Rules for snippets
493	
494	- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
495	- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
496	- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
497	- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
498	- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
499	- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.
500	
501	### Sandbox limits
502	
503	| Limit | Value |
504	|---|---|
505	| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
506	| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
507	| Network and file access | Not documented |
508	| Memory and output size | Not documented |
509	
510	### `code_exec` as a tool
511	
512	`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.
513	
514	## Lifecycle tools
515	
516	A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.
517	
518	| Value | When |
519	|---|---|
520	| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
521	| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
522	| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |
523	
524	Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.
525	
526	```json
527	{
528	  "initial_node": "greeting",
529	  "nodes": {},
530	  "tools": [
531	    {
532	      "type": "function",
533	      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
534	      "function": {
535	        "name": "push_call_result",
536	        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
537	        "parameters": {
538	          "type": "object",
539	          "properties": {
540	            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
541	            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
542	            "body": {
543	              "type": "object",
544	              "properties": {
545	                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
546	                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
547	              }
548	            }
549	          }
550	        }
551	      }
552	    }
553	  ]
554	}
555	```
556	
557	Rules:
558	
559	- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
560	- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
561	- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
562	- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
563	- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
564	- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).
565	
566	## Tool results and the next turn
567	
568	After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:
569	
570	- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
571	- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.
572	
573	What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.
574	
575	Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.
576	
577	## Checklist
578	
579	- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
580	- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
581	- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
582	- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
583	- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
584	- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
585	- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
586	- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
587	- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.
588
